slot.subtopic: Perpendicular distance from point to line
slot.brief: Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from a given point to a line given in symmetric form.

stem: The foot of the perpendicular from $P(4,0,1)$ to the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{1}=\dfrac{z-2}{-2}$ is

verdicts.working: Let the line be A+tv, with A=(1,-1,2) and v=(2,1,-2). Then t=((P-A)·v)/|v|²=9/9=1, so the foot is A+v=(3,0,0).

working:
Let $Q=(1+2t,-1+t,2-2t)$ and $\mathbf d=(2,1,-2)$.\n$(Q-P)\cdot\mathbf d=0\Rightarrow 9t-9=0\Rightarrow t=1$.\nHence $Q=(3,0,0)$.

Independent check: Let the line be A+tv, with A=(1,-1,2) and v=(2,1,-2). Then t=((P-A)·v)/|v|²=9/9=1, so the foot is A+v=(3,0,0).
solution:
Let $Q=(1+2t,-1+t,2-2t)$ be the foot. Since $PQ$ is perpendicular to the line's direction $(2,1,-2)$,
$$(Q-P)\cdot(2,1,-2)=0\Rightarrow 9t-9=0\Rightarrow t=1.$$Hence $Q=(3,0,0)$.
